sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 最中国的时间机器不是钟，是这张圆桌。人可以一年不见，除夕必须把脸凑到同一盏灯下。热气、灯、故意没吃完的鱼，红包和新衣，窗上倒贴的「福」，都在问：你还在不在家里。缺席比吵架更严重——吵架说明你还在这张网上，缺席说明你把「年」过成了别人的节日。视频可以支在酒杯旁，空椅子仍然刺眼。年历翻到腊月三十，城市只做一件事：把人召回来。
sections.en: China's most Chinese time machine is not a clock; it is this round table. People may go a year without meeting, but on New Year's Eve faces must gather under the same lamp. Steam, light, a fish left unfinished on purpose, red envelopes and new clothes, the inverted fu on the window — all ask the same question: are you still in this house? Absence cuts deeper than a quarrel. A quarrel means you are still on the net; absence means you have turned the year into someone else's festival. A video call can sit beside the glasses; the empty chair still stings. When the calendar reaches the thirtieth of the twelfth month, the city does one thing: it calls people back.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 春节把分散的人拉回同一套动作：扫房、贴春联、吃年夜饭、发红包、拜年。农历正月初一是日历上的节日，除夕才是感情的死线。南北菜单不同，规矩相同：必须到场，必须叫人，必须把一年的关系再兑一次现。年不是用来休息的假期，是必须兑现的关系。对在外工作的人，春运再挤也要挤回去，因为「过年」不能只在心里完成。
sections.en: Spring Festival pulls scattered people back into one set of motions: sweeping the house, pasting couplets, the reunion dinner, red envelopes, New Year calls. The first of the first lunar month is a date on the calendar; New Year's Eve is the emotional deadline. Menus differ north and south; the rule does not: you must appear, you must call people by name, you must cash in a year's relationships again. The year is not a holiday for rest. It is a relationship that has to be honoured. For those who work away, the Chunyun crush is still worth boarding, because "passing the year" cannot be done only in the mind.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 在外的人挤春运；在家的人准备房间和菜；回不去的人把手机支在桌上。红包有规矩：结婚的给没结婚的，长辈给晚辈，金额会被比较，里面藏着等级。拜年从磕头变成语音和朋友圈，顺序仍在——先父母，再亲戚，最后同事。南方吃年糕，北方吃饺子，桌上一定有一个「不能吃完」的寓意，鱼就是最常见的那道。孩子挨个叫人、鞠躬，新衣和春联把家里临时变成舞台。
sections.en: Those away squeeze onto Chunyun trains; those at home prepare rooms and dishes; those who cannot return prop a phone on the table. Red envelopes have rules: the married give to the unmarried, elders to juniors, and the sums will be compared — rank lives inside the packet. New Year greetings have shifted from kowtows to voice notes and moments on a feed, yet the order remains: parents first, then relatives, colleagues last. The south eats nian gao, the north dumplings; the table always keeps one dish that must not be finished, and fish is the usual one. Children call names and bow in turn. New clothes and couplets turn the house, for a night, into a stage.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，是被叫乳名、被夹菜，确认自己在家里还有一个位置。家庭这一层，一年的账、病、婚姻会在饭桌上摊开，也在饭桌上暂时和解——团圆既是温暖，也是谈判。社会这一层，十多亿人同时放假，是国家用日历把亲情组织成公共事件。热闹不是装饰，是一种集体证明：这张桌子今年还在，人还没散。
sections.en: At the personal layer, being called by a childhood name and having food placed in your bowl confirms that you still have a place. At the family layer, a year's accounts, illnesses and marriages are spread on the table and, for an evening, half-reconciled — reunion is warmth and a negotiation. At the social layer, more than a billion people holiday at once: the state uses a calendar to organise affection as a public event. The noise is not decoration. It is collective proof that this table still exists this year, and the people have not scattered.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常摩擦是催婚、比孩子、比房子、劝酒，团圆变成一场考核，节日底下是展览。结构问题更硬：买不起票的人、值班的人、和家里关系破裂的人，被节日排除得更明显。越热闹，空椅子越刺眼。视频通话能让声音到场，不能让身体入座。对回不去的人来说，春节不是团圆，是一年一度被提醒自己缺席。
sections.en: The everyday friction is marriage-pushing, comparing children and apartments, pressing drinks: reunion becomes an exam, the festival a display. The structural problem is harder. People who cannot afford a ticket, who are on duty, who have broken with the family, are more visibly shut out by the holiday. The merrier it is, the sharper the empty chair. A video call can deliver a voice; it cannot seat a body. For those who cannot go back, Spring Festival is not reunion. It is the annual reminder of their own absence.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 禁燃烟花以后，空气更干净，夜空却空了一截，有人觉得失落。春节档电影成为新仪式，全家一起进影院，也算一种团圆。反向春运在增加：父母来城市过年，不再强迫年轻人挤回家。国际学生在国外煮一顿饺子，是把年缩小成一口锅。寺庙祈福、花市、庙会是城市的公共年。离婚后的孩子，要在两张桌子之间分配自己。
sections.en: After the fireworks ban the air is cleaner, yet the night sky has a missing piece, and some people feel the loss. The New Year film season has become a new rite: a family in a cinema still counts as reunion. Reverse Chunyun is growing — parents come to the city, and the young are not forced onto the crush home. An international student boiling one pot of dumplings abroad shrinks the year to a single pan. Temple visits, flower markets and temple fairs are the city's public year. After a divorce, a child must divide the self between two tables.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙圣诞夜和三王节也强制团圆，礼物和弥撒是他们的春联与红包。更通用的锚，是任何「一年必须回家一次」的节日：人用一场饭，证明自己还属于某处。挂钩 Experiences：人如何用一顿饭把一年过完、把关系续上。我的立场很清楚——团圆值得保护，催婚、比房、劝酒这些考核可以留在门外。回家是为了被叫乳名，不是为了交一份成绩单。
sections.en: Spanish Nochebuena and Three Kings' Day also force reunion; gifts and mass are their couplets and red envelopes. A more general anchor is any festival that says you must go home once a year: people use a meal to prove they still belong somewhere. Hook it to Experiences: how a dinner closes a year and renews a relationship. My position is clear — reunion is worth protecting; the exam of marriage-pushing, house-comparing and drink-pressing can stay outside the door. You go home to be called by a childhood name, not to hand in a report card.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 中国的节日跟着月亮走，不像公历那样均匀切块。一张年历摊开，是灯、坟、龙舟、月、菊花五种光。元宵的灯笼街道，清明的新土，端午的粽叶，中秋的月饼盒，重阳登山的老人，构成一条可以走的时间河。学生容易把节日报成菜单，考官要听的是：这些日子分别在处理活着的团圆，还是死去的人。同一张脸上，表情会按节气更换。
sections.en: Chinese festivals follow the moon; they are not sliced evenly like the Gregorian year. Spread a calendar and you see five kinds of light: lanterns, graves, dragon boats, the moon, chrysanthemums. Yuanxiao streets, Qingming earth, Duanwu leaves, Mid-Autumn boxes, elders climbing at Chongyang — a river of time you can walk. Students list a menu; examiners want to hear which days handle the reunion of the living, and which handle the dead. On the same face, expression changes with the solar term.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 岁时节日是农业文明留下的操作系统。元宵看灯吃汤圆，在农历正月十五；清明扫墓踏青，有人烧纸钱，希望先人在地下能用；端午包粽子、赛龙舟；中秋赏月吃月饼；重阳登高敬老，在九月初九。一条年历，就是一部关于时间的诗，也是一部关于谁必须被记住的规定。日子不平均，是因为感情不平均：有的夜晚管团圆，有的白天管死亡。
sections.en: The festival year is an operating system left by an agrarian civilisation. Yuanxiao, the fifteenth of the first lunar month, is lanterns and rice balls. Qingming is tomb-sweeping and a spring walk; some burn joss paper so the ancestors can spend it underground. Duanwu wraps zongzi and races boats. Mid-Autumn watches the moon and eats mooncakes. Chongyang, the ninth of the ninth, climbs high and honours the old. A calendar is a poem about time, and a rule about who must be remembered. The days are uneven because feeling is uneven: some nights govern reunion, some daylight governs death.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 城市人可能只过「能放假的」：清明、端午、中秋。农村和老家把清明当一年最大的家庭会议之一——谁上坟，谁没来，会被记。纸钱、香、水果，是给看不见的亲戚的待客。龙舟和灯会越来越像旅游产品，月饼越来越像公司礼。黄历或手机里的节气提醒还在，商场里的圣诞树却开始和春联抢颜色。过节的人分成两种：放假的，和必须回家的。
sections.en: City people may keep only the festivals that come with a public holiday: Qingming, Duanwu, Mid-Autumn. In the countryside and back home, Qingming is one of the year's largest family meetings — who went to the grave, who did not, will be noted. Joss paper, incense and fruit are hospitality for relatives you cannot see. Dragon boats and lantern fairs look more and more like tourism; mooncakes look more and more like a company gift. Almanacs and phone reminders still mark the solar terms, yet mall Christmas trees now compete in colour with couplets. Festival-goers split in two: those on holiday, and those who must go home.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，身体按年记住甜、苦、冷、圆：汤圆、粽叶、月饼、菊花，都是可吃的日历。家庭这一层，活人和死人被定期召回同一套动作，上完坟去踏青，生死挨着。社会这一层，公共假期让全国同时减速，文化记忆不必只靠课本。节日把「记得谁」写成日期，比口号更难删除。
sections.en: At the personal layer the body remembers, year by year, sweet, bitter, cold and round: rice balls, zongzi leaves, mooncakes, chrysanthemums — an edible calendar. At the family layer the living and the dead are called back, on a schedule, into the same motions; a spring walk follows the grave, life and death side by side. At the social layer, public holidays slow the whole country at once, so cultural memory need not live only in textbooks. A festival writes "whom we remember" as a date, harder to delete than a slogan.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是月饼盒比馅贵，节日变成快递、礼盒和浪费。结构更冷：不回家、不信烧纸、没有家族墓地的人，会被说「没根」。旅游化让仪式好看，也可能把先人变成背景板。龙舟鼓和灯会卖得出票，却不一定还连着原来要纪念的人。节日一旦只剩货架，年历就从规定变成购物清单。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is a box that costs more than the filling: festivals become parcels, gift tins and waste. The structure is colder. People who do not go home, who do not burn paper, who have no family grave, are told they have "no roots". Tourism makes ritual photogenic, and can turn ancestors into a backdrop. Dragon-boat drums and lantern fairs can sell tickets without still being tied to the person they once commemorated. Once a festival is only a shelf, the calendar has become a shopping list.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 少数民族节日，比如泼水和火把，提醒中国不是一套年历。七夕被写成中国情人节，是新发明。冬至在南方仍比新年更像「必须吃」的日子。西方十二月二十四到二十五进入商场，形成双重年。年轻人用露营替代上坟后的踏青。非遗申请让地方节日互相竞争，谁申上，谁就被旅游看见。
sections.en: Minority festivals — water-splashing, torch festivals — remind you that China is not one calendar. Qixi written as "Chinese Valentine's Day" is a recent invention. In the south, the winter solstice still feels more like a day you must eat than the New Year does. 24–25 December have entered the malls, making a double year. Young people replace the post-grave spring walk with camping. Intangible-heritage applications set local festivals competing: whoever is listed is seen by tourism.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙的 Semana Santa 处理神圣与死亡，圣诞处理团圆，万灵节上坟——对应清明的那一层。节日教人如何过一年，也教人如何跟死者共处。挂钩 Experiences：人用日期组织感情，决定谁必须被召回。我的立场是：可以不烧纸，形式可以改；但不能把记得的人从年历上删掉。记得，比仪式的外观更重要。
sections.en: Spain's Semana Santa handles the sacred and death, Christmas handles reunion, All Saints' Day visits graves — that last layer maps onto Qingming. Festivals teach you how to live a year, and how to live with the dead. Hook it to Experiences: people organise feeling as dates, and decide who must be called back. My position: you need not burn paper, and the form may change; you may not delete the remembered from the calendar. Remembering matters more than how the rite looks.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 中国人用酒席标记人生。孩子满月要请客，红蛋和签名簿把一个婴儿公开；一周岁抓周，桌上摆钱、笔、书、乐器、算盘，看孩子抓什么，家人就笑着说这是兴趣或天赋。婚礼上要敬茶、改口；六十或八十要办寿宴，长寿面和金是给镜头的。礼金簿、摄影师、司仪都在场。镜头里是蛋糕，底下是一份公开声明：这个人被承认了。
sections.en: Chinese life is marked with banquets. A full-month feast makes a baby public with red eggs and a signing book. At one year, zhuazhou: money, a pen, books, an instrument, an abacus are laid out, and whatever the child grabs, the family smiles and calls it interest or talent. Weddings require serving tea and changing how you address the parents; at sixty or eighty a longevity banquet is due, noodles and gold for the camera. The gift ledger, photographer and emcee are all present. The lens sees cake. Underneath is a public statement: this person has been recognised.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 人生礼仪把私人时间变成公共事件。不被请客，等于还不存在于亲戚的地图上。抓周不是测试智商，是家庭把期待摆上桌，让偶然变成可以讲很多年的故事。满月、婚礼、寿宴，都在当众回答同一个问题：我们现在算什么关系。仪式要有见证者，所以必须吵、必须拍、必须发。一生不是自己过完的，是被别人看着过完的。
sections.en: Life-cycle rites turn private time into a public event. Not to be invited is not yet to exist on the relatives' map. Zhuazhou is not an IQ test; it is a family laying its hopes on a table and letting chance become a story that can be told for years. The full-month feast, the wedding, the longevity banquet all answer, in public, the same question: what are we to one another now? A rite needs witnesses, so it must be loud, photographed, posted. A life is not finished by oneself. It is finished while others watch.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 谁出钱，谁就有权决定桌数和菜单。满月常是祖辈的戏；婚礼是两家谈判彩礼、婚房、户口；寿宴是子女的孝心表演，也是老人还活着、还能坐上座的证明。城市酒店承办，农村流水席。酒店大厅的背景板写着名字和日期，没被邀请但同村的人会在门外看。孩子在闪光灯下哭，大人笑着解释「这是天赋」。
sections.en: Whoever pays decides the number of tables and the menu. The full-month feast is often the grandparents' play; a wedding is two families negotiating betrothal gifts, a marital home, household registration; a longevity banquet is the children's performance of filial piety, and proof that the elder is still alive and can still take the seat of honour. Cities hire hotels; villages run flowing banquet tables. A hotel backdrop prints a name and a date; villagers not invited watch from the door. The child cries under flash; adults smile and explain that this is talent.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，是被一群人叫名字，确认阶段已经转换：婴儿成为孩子，两人成为亲戚，老人成为还坐得住的寿星。家庭这一层，礼物和礼金让互助可见，来往被记在簿子上。社会这一层，用一套可重复的剧本降低「我们现在算什么关系」的不确定性。酒席吵，是因为承认需要声音。
sections.en: At the personal layer, a crowd calling your name confirms that a stage has changed: an infant becomes a child, two people become kin, an elder becomes a longevity guest still able to sit. At the family layer, gifts and cash envelopes make mutual aid visible; coming and going are written in a ledger. At the social layer, a repeatable script lowers the uncertainty of "what are we now". Banquets are loud because recognition needs a voice.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是份子钱、攀比桌数、孩子在闪光灯下哭，仪式变成消费。结构更硬：办不起的人、不婚的人、没有儿子办寿的人，会被当成人生不完整。抓周的「天赋」故事，可能变成一辈子的剧本，把一次偶然写成命运。见证一旦变成债务，来参加的人就不再是亲戚，而是债权人。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is gift-money, competing over table counts, a child crying under flash: ritual becomes consumption. The structure is harder. People who cannot afford a feast, who do not marry, who have no son to host a longevity banquet, are treated as incomplete lives. The zhuazhou "talent" story can become a lifelong script, writing chance as fate. Once witnessing turns into debt, the guests are no longer relatives. They are creditors.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 丧礼比婚礼更能看见等级：谁到场、谁送什么，比喜酒更诚实。新式婚礼司仪在发明传统，把节目单写成「古礼」。同性伴侣缺少公共仪式，地图上仍是空白。月子中心、婚庆公司把人生仪仗商业化。抓周道具更新成鼠标、护照。不办酒改发红包，关系仍要记账——形式变了，承认的需求没变。
sections.en: A funeral shows rank more clearly than a wedding: who comes, who gives what, is more honest than a happy banquet. New-style wedding emcees invent tradition, writing a programme as "ancient rite". Same-sex partners still lack a public ceremony; the map has a blank. Confinement centres and wedding companies commercialise the escort of a life. Zhuazhou props update to a mouse and a passport. Skip the banquet, send a red envelope: the relationship is still entered in a ledger. The form changed; the need to be recognised did not.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙有洗礼、初领圣体、婚礼和寿辰，更常把这些时刻送进教堂；中国更常送进酒店和村口的流水席。挂钩 Experiences：一生不是自己过完的，是被别人见证着过完的。我的立场是：仪式可以简化，见证不能取消；但见证不该变成债务。被叫名字就够了，不必比谁的桌数更多。
sections.en: Spain has baptism, first communion, weddings and birthday feasts, more often walked into a church; China more often walks them into a hotel or a village flowing banquet. Hook it to Experiences: a life is not finished by oneself; it is finished while being witnessed. My position: the rite may be simplified, witnessing cannot be cancelled — but witnessing should not become debt. Being called by name is enough. There is no need to compete over who has more tables.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 中国式待客有一套看不见的剧本：客人进门先换鞋，或被让到上座；茶和瓜子马上出现；饭桌上主人不停夹菜，客人举手挡；「吃好了」之后，主人还会再劝一碗。厨房里往往还有没端出来的菜。酒杯对碰，目光要接住。孩子被叫出来打招呼。送客要送到电梯或巷口。两边都在演戏，戏的名字叫尊重。
sections.en: Chinese hosting has an invisible script. Guests change shoes at the door, or are shown to the seat of honour; tea and melon seeds appear at once; at table the host keeps placing food, the guest raises a hand to fend it off; after "I'm full", another bowl is still urged. The kitchen often still holds dishes not yet brought out. Glasses meet, and the eyes must meet too. A child is called out to greet. Guests are seen off as far as the lift or the lane. Both sides are acting. The play is called respect.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 待客不是服务态度，是把客人暂时编进家里的等级和面子。菜的数量在说「你值得」；推辞在说「我不敢当」。演砸了——吃太光，或一口不动——都会让主人没面子。热情必须被看见，客气也必须被看见，两套动作互相完成。待客是把时间献给别人的组织法：这一顿饭不属于效率，属于关系。
sections.en: Hosting is not a service smile. It is folding a guest, for a while, into the household's rank and face. The number of dishes says "you are worth this"; the polite refusal says "I dare not accept so much". Bungle the play — eat the table bare, or not touch a bite — and the host loses face. Warmth must be seen, and so must modesty; the two motions complete each other. Hosting is a way of organising time as a gift to someone else. This meal does not belong to efficiency. It belongs to a relationship.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 谁坐上座，谁夹第一筷，谁买单，都有默认答案。家庭待客看厨房还在不在忙；商务待客看包间和酒。过敏、素食、不喝酒，是对新剧本的压力测试：好的主人会换菜，差的主人会说「就一点」。送客的距离衡量关系有多近——送到门口是礼貌，送到巷口是真心。外卖和酒店可以替代家庭厨房，但剧本还在。
sections.en: Who takes the seat of honour, who takes the first chopstick, who pays: each has a default answer. Family hosting is read in whether the kitchen is still busy; business hosting is read in a private room and the liquor. Allergy, vegetarianism, not drinking — these pressure-test the new script. A good host changes the dish; a poor one says "just a little". How far you walk a guest measures closeness: to the door is manners, to the lane is feeling. Delivery and hotels can replace a family kitchen. The script remains.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，被照顾的感觉具体到筷子和热茶，人被安放在上座。群体这一层，主客共同完成一出戏，关系被确认：我们会演，说明我们还是自己人。社会这一层，把慷慨训练成美德，让陌生人也能进门。好客不是性格，是一种可以被学习的公共技术。一碗再劝的汤，把「你值得」说成动作。
sections.en: At the personal layer, being cared for is as concrete as chopsticks and hot tea; a person is placed in the seat of honour. At the group layer, host and guest finish a play together, and the relationship is confirmed: we can act this, therefore we are still our own people. At the social layer, generosity is trained as a virtue, so that a stranger can still come through the door. Hospitality is not a personality. It is a public technique that can be learned.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是浪费、劝酒、客人吃撑，热情变成负担。结构问题是：不会演戏的人——外国人、怕社交的人、钱不够的人——被当成不懂事。待客也可以变成权力：我请你，你欠我；账单确认地位。强迫不是好客。一套剧本如果容不下过敏和素食，它保护的是面子，不是客人。真正的尊重，是让客人有台阶下。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is waste, drink-pressing, guests stuffed: warmth becomes a burden. The structural problem is that people who cannot act the play — foreigners, the socially anxious, those without money — are treated as not knowing how to behave. Hosting can also become power: I treat you, you owe me; the bill confirms rank. Coercion is not hospitality. If a script cannot make room for an allergy or a vegetarian, it is protecting face, not the guest.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 外卖和私厨在改家庭厨房的地位，待客不一定还闻得到油烟。AA 制在年轻人里生长，被长辈看成薄情。直播探店把待客审美公开展示，夹菜和摆盘都成为表演。清真和素食挑战默认菜单，好不好客要看主人会不会换菜。民宿、茶室把待客职业化，热情变成可以购买的服务。
sections.en: Delivery and private chefs are changing the family kitchen's place; hosting may no longer smell of cooking oil. Going Dutch is growing among the young, and elders read it as thin feeling. Livestream restaurant visits put hosting aesthetics on public display; serving food and plating become performance. Halal and vegetarian tables challenge the default menu: whether you are a good host is whether you will change a dish. Guesthouses and tea rooms professionalise hosting; warmth becomes a service you can buy.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙的小食和劝「再来一点」很像夹菜，热情同样具体到盘子；但酒更常是自己倒，账单有时 AA，不必把欠写进下一顿。挂钩 Experiences：待客是把时间献给别人的组织法。我的立场是：热情可以真，强迫不算好客。客人说「吃好了」，应该被当成答案，而不是下一碗的开始。
sections.en: Spanish tapas and the push to have "just a little more" resemble serving food onto another's plate; warmth is equally concrete, down to the dish. But wine is more often poured for oneself, and the bill is sometimes split — debt need not be written into the next meal. Hook it to Experiences: hosting is a way of organising time as a gift to someone else. My position: warmth can be real; coercion does not count as hospitality. When a guest says "I'm full", that should be an answer, not the start of the next bowl.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 茶在中国不是一种饮料那么简单。它可以是四月山坡上的龙井，叶子站在玻璃杯里；可以是泡了十年的普洱，饼上印着年份；也可以是街上那杯加了奶和珍珠的东西。紫砂壶、公道杯、闻香杯，或便利店冰茶、办公室大杯续水，是同一种叶子走进三种时间。第一泡常被倒掉。茶农还在四月的节气里采茶。
sections.en: Tea in China is not merely a drink. It can be April Longjing from a hillside, leaves standing in a glass; it can be puer steeped for ten years, a year stamped on the cake; it can be that cup on the street with milk and pearls. A zisha pot, a fairness pitcher, an aroma cup — or iced tea from a shop, a large office mug kept refilled — are the same leaf walking into three kinds of time. The first infusion is often poured away. Tea farmers are still picking inside April's solar terms.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 绿茶——龙井、毛峰——讲究产地和鲜，清明前后的春茶最被珍视，四月是它们的季节。红茶全发酵，味道更稳。乌龙在中间。普洱论年份，像酒。花茶常被当成「茶饮料」：茉莉、菊花，香气先于茶味。功夫茶是一种把时间切成小泡的技术。怎么泡，决定你在演哪一出：鲜、发酵，还是陈年。
sections.en: Green teas — Longjing, Maofeng — prize origin and freshness. Spring tea around Qingming is treasured most; April is their season. Black tea is fully oxidised and steadier. Oolong sits in between. Puer is sold by year, like wine. Scented teas often drink as "tea beverages": jasmine, chrysanthemum, aroma ahead of the leaf. Gongfu tea is a technique for slicing time into small infusions. How you brew decides which play you are in: freshness, fermentation, or age.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 茶农和节气绑在一起，采的是山和天气；茶商卖山头和故事；办公室用茶替代咖啡因，杯子一直在续；家庭用茶开场待客。怎么泡决定场合：盖碗、紫砂，还是一次性杯子。年轻人更多进茶饮店，把茶当成甜和社交，不是苦和静。同一片叶子，可以是仪式，也可以是排队时那杯冰的。
sections.en: Tea farmers are bound to the solar terms; what they pick is mountain and weather. Merchants sell a hillside and a story. Offices use tea as caffeine, the mug endlessly refilled. Families open hospitality with tea. How you brew decides the occasion: a gaiwan, zisha, or a disposable cup. Young people more often walk into tea-drink shops, taking tea as sweetness and social life, not bitterness and quiet. The same leaf can be a rite, or the iced cup you hold in a queue.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，手被泡茶训练得慢下来，第一泡倒掉也是一种停顿。群体这一层，一壶茶让谈话有了合法的间隙，不必用酒去填。社会这一层，产地、年份、品种构成一套品味语言，像红酒一样可以谈论身份。茶把一小时的速度交还给喝的人，让这一小时可以快，也可以慢。
sections.en: At the personal layer, the hands are trained by brewing to slow down; pouring away the first infusion is itself a pause. At the group layer, a pot of tea gives talk a lawful gap, which need not be filled with liquor. At the social layer, origin, year and variety make a language of taste, like wine, in which identity can be discussed. Tea hands the speed of an hour back to the drinker, so that the hour may be fast or slow.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是茶桌变成炫耀山头的竞赛，谁喝得更「正」、更贵。结构更刺：春茶被炒成金融产品，茶农不一定喝得起自己的四月；奶茶的糖在改「茶」的身体含义，苦和静被甜和排队替换。当叶子只剩下价格，产地就不再是土地，而是标签。慢一旦被删掉，茶就只是咖啡因。四月本该属于山坡，不属于炒作。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is a tea table turned into a contest of hillsides: who drinks the more "authentic", the more expensive. The structure cuts deeper. Spring tea is speculated as a financial product; farmers may not be able to afford their own April. The sugar in milk tea rewrites what tea does to a body; bitterness and quiet are replaced by sweetness and a queue. When a leaf is only a price, origin is no longer land. It is a label. Once slowness is deleted, tea is only caffeine.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 茶马古道连着边疆；成都茶馆仍是公共空间，一壶茶可以坐一下午。茶与禅、与文人的旧关系还在课本里。罐装茶和袋泡茶让茶民主化，办公室人人可续杯。咖啡店在争夺原来属于茶馆的座位。新茶饮出海，把珍珠和糖写成中国茶的新名片，也把「慢」留在了山坡上。四月的叶子，和街上的糖，正在抢同一句「茶」。
sections.en: The old tea-horse roads still touch the frontier. Chengdu teahouses remain public space: one pot can last an afternoon. Tea's old ties to Chan and to scholars still live in textbooks. Canned tea and tea bags democratise the leaf; everyone in an office can refill. Coffee shops compete for the seats that once belonged to teahouses. New tea drinks go overseas, writing pearls and sugar as China's new tea card, and leaving slowness on the hillside.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 南欧用咖啡和红酒标记时间和身份，年份与产地的语言几乎可直接翻译到普洱。咖啡让人快，红酒让人坐下来，茶可以选择做哪一种。挂钩 Experiences：人用一杯东西，决定这一小时是快还是慢。我的立场是：茶可以甜，也可以排队；但不能把「慢」完全从文化里删掉。第一泡倒掉，是为了还记得时间。
sections.en: Southern Europe marks time and identity with coffee and wine; the language of year and origin translates almost directly onto puer. Coffee makes people fast, wine makes them sit; tea can choose which to be. Hook it to Experiences: people use a cup to decide whether this hour is fast or slow. My position: tea may be sweet, and it may be queued for; slowness must not be deleted from the culture entirely. The first infusion is poured away so that time is still remembered.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 中国疾控中心 2024 年全国调查（2026 年发表）显示：15 岁及以上过去一年喝过酒的占 27.6%，过去 30 天占 20.3%；男性 44.5%，女性 10.2%。数字先破神话——不是人人都喝。照片里的酒桌却常常像人人都喝：很小的白酒杯、同时在场的啤酒红酒洋酒、有人站起来敬主位，有人把酒倒进植物。这之间的缝，就是面子。
sections.en: A 2024 China CDC national survey, published in 2026, found that among people aged 15 and over, 27.6% had drunk in the past year and 20.3% in the past 30 days; 44.5% of men, 10.2% of women. The numbers break a myth first: not everyone drinks. The table in the photograph, though, often looks as if everyone does — tiny baijiu cups, beer and wine and spirits present at once, someone standing to toast the host's seat, someone pouring a drink into a plant. The seam between the two is face.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 酒在中国常常不是口味，是位置。啤酒、白酒、洋酒、红酒四种道具，白酒最像仪式：杯小、酒烈、话重。「干杯」时眼睛要看人。劝酒有时是热情，有时是权力测试：你喝，就是给我面子；你不喝，就是当众拆我。酒桌把忠诚写成酒量，把拒绝写成失礼。喝什么，就是选择加入哪一张桌子。
sections.en: In China, drink is often not a taste. It is a position. Beer, baijiu, spirits, wine — four props, and baijiu is the most like ritual: small cup, strong liquor, heavy words. At "ganbei" the eyes have to meet. Pressing a drink is sometimes warmth, sometimes a test of power: if you drink, you give me face; if you refuse, you dismantle me in public. The table writes loyalty as drinking capacity, and refusal as rudeness. What you drink is which table you choose to join.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 商务和婚礼最难逃。主位先举，按地位走。不会喝的人「努力喝一点点」，是面子课里已经碰过的句子。女性被允许少喝，杯里颜色更浅或改喝茶，也被排除在真正的决定之外。年轻人用「开车」「过敏」「明天考试」当通行证，效果取决于桌上谁更大。门外总有透气、醒酒的人，账单和空瓶留在桌上。
sections.en: Business dinners and weddings are the hardest to escape. The host's seat raises first; the round follows rank. "I'll try a little" from someone who does not drink is a sentence already met in the lesson on face. Women are allowed to drink less — paler glasses, or tea instead — and are also shut out of the real decisions. The young use "I'm driving", "I'm allergic", "I have an exam tomorrow" as passes; whether they work depends on who is bigger at the table. Outside there are always people getting air, sobering up. The bill and the empty bottles stay on the table.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，酒能让不好意思说的话出口。群体这一层，共同醉一次，像短暂结盟，第二天还记得谁陪了谁。社会这一层，在正式合同之外，用身体完成信任的表演：干杯被当成签字。酒把一个夜晚组织成关系，让生人很快变成「喝过的人」。27.6% 说明酒常见，但不是唯一入口。
sections.en: At the personal layer, drink can let out words that were too awkward to say. At the group layer, getting drunk together is a brief alliance; the next day you still remember who sat with whom. At the social layer, outside the formal contract, the body performs trust: emptying a cup is treated as a signature. Drink organises a night into a relationship, and turns strangers quickly into people you have drunk with. 27.6% shows that drinking is common. It is not the only door.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是伤身、出丑、第二天后悔，连续应酬最伤身。结构是：不喝的人升迁变慢；酒驾把一桌热情变成事故；把忠诚写成酒量，是一种很不健康的组织法。女性少喝既是保护，也是把核心局关在门外。27.6% 说明多数人并不靠酒过社会，酒桌却仍像唯一入口。拒绝不该是失礼的唯一解释。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is harm to the body, embarrassment, regret the next morning; a run of work banquets harms the body most. The structure is that those who do not drink are promoted more slowly; drink-driving turns a table's warmth into an accident; writing loyalty as capacity is an unhealthy way to organise people. Women drinking less is both protection and shutting them out of the inner game. 27.6% shows that most people do not run their social life on alcohol, yet the table still looks like the only door. Refusal should not be the only reading of rudeness.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 禁酒令进入校园和公务，公开场合越来越不能灌。精酿酒吧把酒拉回口味，喝的是香气不是效忠。解酒药和代喝是灰色服务，有人花钱请人代喝。地方酒被金融化，瓶子变成投资。宗教戒酒提供另一套拒绝的语言。直播喝酒打赏制造新的羞耻，醉从饭桌搬到屏幕上，观众为灌酒付钱。
sections.en: Alcohol bans have entered campuses and official life; public pouring is less and less allowed. Craft bars pull drink back toward taste: you drink aroma, not allegiance. Hangover pills and paid stand-in drinkers are a grey service; some people pay others to drink for them. Local liquors are financialised; the bottle becomes an investment. Religious abstinence offers another language of refusal. Livestream drinking for tips invents a new shame: drunkenness moves from the table to the screen, and the audience pays for the pouring.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙红酒配餐、啤酒配足球，醉有时是欢乐不是效忠；账单可以 AA，不必把拒绝写成拆台。挂钩 Experiences：人如何用一杯东西度过一个夜晚、签一场关系。我的立场是：可以喝，不可以把拒绝当成失礼的唯一解释。27.6% 已经说明，不喝的人不是例外，男 44.5%、女 10.2% 的差距也说明局是被组织出来的。
sections.en: In Spain wine goes with the meal, beer with football; drunkenness is sometimes joy, not allegiance. The bill may be split; a refusal need not be written as wrecking the table. Hook it to Experiences: how people use a cup to get through a night and to sign a relationship. My position: you may drink; you may not treat refusal as the only reading of rudeness. 27.6% already shows that non-drinkers are not the exception, and the gap — 44.5% of men, 10.2% of women — shows that the inner game is organised.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 中国菜不是一种味道。圆桌转盘上，十道菜围着主食：辣椒、花椒，或清蒸鱼的蒸汽；米饭、面条、包子、馒头，总有一种在场。筷子是工具，也是节奏，公筷和汤碗是新规矩。街边摊的烟和塑料凳，菜单上的方言菜名，有人拍照，有人已经伸筷。厨房门口流水和叫号。一张桌子，就是一张可以走的地图。
sections.en: Chinese food is not one taste. On a round table's lazy Susan, ten dishes surround the staple: chilli and Sichuan pepper, or steam off a whole fish. Rice, noodles, bao, mantou — one of them is always present. Chopsticks are a tool and a tempo; serving chopsticks and soup bowls are the new rule. Smoke from a stall, plastic stools, dish names in dialect; someone photographs, someone has already reached. Water runs at the kitchen door, numbers are called. A table is a map you can walk.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 「八大菜系」是一种方便的说法，真实生活更碎。川菜麻辣、粤菜求鲜、鲁菜咸香、淮扬清、杭帮雅，加上街头小吃，构成舌头上的籍贯。南甜北咸是气候和保存，不是性格：开口第一口，别人就知道你从哪来。主食是碳水化合物，菜和汤在周围，零食是另一件事。菜系是地方身份的舌头版。
sections.en: "Eight great cuisines" is a convenient phrase; real life is more broken up. Sichuan numbing-heat, Cantonese freshness, Shandong salt-and-savour, Huaiyang clarity, Hangzhou elegance, plus street snacks — ancestral place on the tongue. Sweet south, salty north is climate and preservation, not character: the first bite tells others where you come from. Staples are carbohydrates; dishes and soups sit around them; snacks are another matter. A cuisine school is local identity in a tongue version.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 家庭日常可能很素、很快；请客一定更油、更满，劝菜开始上演。火锅把煮的过程变成聚会本身，人人伸筷，不必同一盘。移民把辣带进北方，把奶茶带进所有车站。猪肉价格能改变桌上的肉；豪华食材在表演另一种菜系：钱。外卖改味觉，预制菜让人怀疑「还是不是那家店」。谁在吃什么，比八大菜系的名单更真实。
sections.en: Family everyday eating may be plain and fast; hosting is always oilier and fuller, and serving onto others' plates begins. Hotpot turns the act of cooking into the gathering itself; everyone reaches, without sharing one finished plate. Migrants carry chilli into the north, and milk tea into every station. The price of pork can change the meat on the table; luxury ingredients perform another cuisine: money. Delivery rewrites the palate; pre-made dishes make people wonder whether this is still that restaurant. Who is eating what is more real than the list of eight schools.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，家乡味是身体的护照，出国以后最想吃的那一口会说明身份。群体这一层，共食一张转盘，比分餐更像结盟。社会这一层，地方菜是旅游和软实力，也是方言之外的识别码。一顿饭把一天两次的进食，过成「我从哪来」。南甜北咸让地图可以尝，而不只是看。
sections.en: At the personal layer, hometown flavour is a passport in the body; the bite you miss most abroad will say who you are. At the group layer, eating from one lazy Susan is more like an alliance than eating from separate plates. At the social layer, regional food is tourism and soft power, and an identity code besides dialect. A meal turns eating twice a day into "where I come from". Sweet south, salty north lets the map be tasted, not only seen.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是劝菜、浪费、口味霸权——全桌必须辣，不辣的人没有位置。结构是：真正的街头摊贩被卫生和租金赶走，菜系变成商场里的表演；油盐对身体的账单后到。光盘行动在对抗面子式浪费，但转盘仍鼓励点得过多。保护地方味，不等于强迫全桌同一辣度。南甜北咸可以并存。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is serving onto others' plates, waste, and a tyranny of taste — the whole table must be spicy, and those who cannot take heat have no place. The structure is that real street vendors are pushed out by hygiene rules and rent, and cuisine becomes a performance in a mall; oil and salt send the body's bill later. The clean-plate campaign fights waste-as-face, yet the lazy Susan still encourages ordering too much. Protecting a local taste is not the same as forcing one chilli level on the table. Sweet south and salty north can sit together.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 素食、清真、过敏正在改默认菜单。网红店和排队把味道写成流量。预制菜进餐厅带来信任危机。筷子与刀叉是不同的身体训练，节奏不一样。「光盘行动」把吃光写成美德，对抗剩菜里的面子。外卖让一个人也能吃火锅，却吃不到转盘上的结盟。地方味在变，识别码还在。
sections.en: Vegetarian, halal and allergy needs are changing the default menu. Viral restaurants and queues write flavour as traffic. Pre-made dishes entering kitchens bring a crisis of trust. Chopsticks and forks train the body differently; the tempo is not the same. The clean-plate campaign writes eating everything as virtue, against the face inside leftovers. Delivery lets one person eat hotpot alone, but not the alliance on a lazy Susan. Local taste is changing; the identity code remains.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙有地域菜和火腿语言，小盘是小盘社交，中国转盘是大盘社交：一个把选择留给个人，一个把关系煮在同一锅。挂钩 Experiences：人如何把一天两次的进食，过成身份和关系。我的立场是：保护地方味，不等于强迫全桌同一辣度。南甜北咸可以并存，不必谁征服谁。火锅已经示范了另一种共食。
sections.en: Spain has regional cooking and a language of ham; small plates are small-plate social life, the Chinese lazy Susan is large-plate social life. One leaves choice with the person; the other cooks the relationship in one pot. Hook it to Experiences: how people turn eating twice a day into identity and relationship. My position: protecting a local taste is not forcing one chilli level on the whole table. Sweet south and salty north can coexist; neither need conquer the other. Hotpot already shows another way of eating together.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 长城的墙在山脊上，人有时比砖更显眼；故宫中轴通向黄色屋顶，安检队伍排到门外；兵马俑一张张不同的脸停在土里。江南古镇的酒吧招牌亮着，原住民走后门。自拍杆、讲解旗、耳机争夺同一段声音。「不到长城非好汉」写在标牌上，门票、安检、限流通知写在另一张纸上。国宝在玻璃后，人在玻璃外证明「我来过」。
sections.en: The Wall sits on a ridge; people are sometimes more visible than bricks. The Forbidden City's axis runs toward yellow roofs, the security queue out the gate. Terracotta faces, each different, wait in the earth. In a Jiangnan old town the bar signs are lit; original residents use the back door. Selfie sticks, a guide's flag, earphones fight for the same stretch of sound. "He who has not been to the Great Wall is no true hero" is on a sign; tickets, checks and visitor-cap notices are on another sheet. Treasures sit behind glass; people outside it prove "I was here".

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 名胜古迹把历史折叠成可以走路的空间。「故」是过去，「宫」是权力，「故事」是我们被要求记住的版本。长城、故宫、兵马俑、江南古镇，是中国旅行的「必背课文」。它们漂亮，也拥挤。旅游是 Experiences，但谁有权解释这块砖，已经是文化政治。好的游览不是打卡，而是把地方读成文本：墙为什么修在山脊上。
sections.en: Famous places fold history into space you can walk. Gu is the past, gong is power, gushi is the version we are asked to remember. The Wall, the Forbidden City, the terracotta army, Jiangnan old towns — the set texts of China travel. They are beautiful and crowded. Tourism is Experiences, but who has the right to explain this brick is already cultural politics. A good visit is not a check-in. It is reading a place as a text: why a wall was built on a ridge.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 国内游客用假期和高考后的夏天；国际游客用名单；当地人用后门和清晨。讲解员、黄牛、直播在争夺同一段城墙的声音。国宝在玻璃后，人在玻璃外拍照。热门景点开始限流，门票本身成为筛选。打卡路线把身体带过去，不一定把理解带回来。谁被旅游看见，谁就被写成「中国」；谁住在后门，谁就从画面里消失。
sections.en: Domestic visitors use holidays and the summer after gaokao; international visitors use a list; locals use the back door and early morning. Guides, scalpers and livestreams fight for the same stretch of wall's voice. Treasures sit behind glass; people photograph from outside it. Popular sites have begun capping visitors; the ticket itself becomes a filter. A check-in route can carry a body there without carrying understanding back. Whoever tourism sees is written as "China"; whoever lives at the back door disappears from the frame.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，身体走进课本，墙和陶脸不再只是纸上的词。群体这一层，家庭用旅行制造共同记忆：我们一起爬过、一起排过队。社会这一层，遗产成为认同和外交的展示柜，世界遗产名录是国家的成绩单。去过，就有了一句可以对外说的句子。中轴和不同的陶脸，比打卡更值得带走。
sections.en: At the personal layer the body walks into the textbook; walls and clay faces are no longer only words on paper. At the group layer, families manufacture shared memory with a trip: we climbed, we queued. At the social layer, heritage becomes a display case for identity and diplomacy; the World Heritage list is a national report card. Having been, you have a sentence you can say outward. The axis and the different clay faces are more worth taking home than a check-in.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是人多到看不见墙，自拍杆比城砖更近。结构是：古镇原住民被租金搬走，留下布景；「不到长城非好汉」把体力、门票和假期当成爱国测试。打卡完成，理解缺席。如果一个地方只剩游客，它还是文化吗？文化需要人住着，不只是人路过。好汉叙事把去过写成合格。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is a crowd so thick the wall disappears, the selfie stick closer than the brick. The structure is that original residents of old towns are priced out by rent, leaving a stage set; "no true hero without the Wall" turns stamina, a ticket and a holiday into a patriotism test. The check-in is done; understanding is absent. If a place is left with only tourists, is it still culture? Culture needs people living in it, not only passing through. The hero story writes having-been as a pass mark.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 世界遗产名录的竞争让地方互相抢叙事。数字复制与开放让人在屏幕上先看一遍。红色旅游把革命遗址写成路线。过度旅游逼出限流。文物返还争议提醒：玻璃后的国宝，所有权并不安静。本地讲解和国家叙事不总是同一句话，墙的声音有人在争。博物馆把私人的手艺变成公共记忆。
sections.en: Competition for the World Heritage list sets places fighting over narrative. Digital copies and open access let people see a site on a screen first. Red tourism writes revolutionary sites as a route. Overtourism forces visitor caps. Disputes over returning artefacts remind you that treasures behind glass do not sit quietly in ownership. Local commentary and the national story are not always the same sentence; people fight for the wall's voice. Museums turn private craft into public memory.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙有阿尔罕布拉、圣地亚哥之路，同样要处理人流和「谁的故事」：游客要美，住着的人要生活。挂钩 Experiences：旅行是把一生中的几天，交给一块被规定为重要的地方。我的立场是：去可以，打卡不够，要能说出墙为什么在这里。「不到长城非好汉」可以是邀请，不该是压力。去了，要能解释。
sections.en: Spain has the Alhambra and the Camino de Santiago, and the same problems of crowds and whose story it is: visitors want beauty, people who live there want a life. Hook it to Experiences: travel is handing several days of a life to a place that has been ruled important. My position: going is allowed; checking in is not enough — you should be able to say why the wall is here. "No true hero without the Wall" can be an invitation. It should not be pressure. Having gone, you should be able to explain.

sections.title: 画面与现象
sections.zh: 春运是春节前后的大规模回家潮。火车站候车大厅的人潮和行李箱，电子屏上的晚点与候补，羽绒服、编织袋、挂在胸前的票，站台上的热气和广播，组成一种只在那时出现的国家风景。家长举着接人的纸板，高铁过道里站着人，孩子睡在行李上。高铁让路程变短，车票仍然紧张。那不是度假的画面，是交人的画面。
sections.en: Chunyun is the vast homeward rush around Spring Festival. Station halls of crowds and suitcases, delays and waitlists on the board, down coats, woven bags, a ticket hung on the chest, steam and loudspeakers on the platform — a national landscape that exists only then. Parents hold cardboard signs; people stand in high-speed aisles; a child sleeps on the luggage. Rail shortened the road; tickets stay tight. That is not a holiday picture. It is a picture of handing a person back.

sections.title: 这是什么
sections.zh: 春运是日历、家庭和交通系统叠在一起的组织事件。它证明：在中国，一段关系强到可以让几百万人次同时移动。Experiences 在这里不是「旅行好不好玩」，是「你被要求出现在哪里」。对农民工和在大城市上班的年轻人，回家不是度假，是把一年的自己交回去给父母看一眼。票是通行证，家是考场。被看见，年才算过完。
sections.en: Chunyun is an organised event in which calendar, family and the transport system are stacked. It proves that in China a relationship can be strong enough to move millions of journeys at once. Experiences here is not whether the trip was pleasant. It is where you are required to appear. For migrant workers and young people in big cities, going home is not a holiday. It is handing a year's self back to parents for a look. The ticket is a pass; home is an examination hall. Until you are seen, the year is not finished.

sections.title: 谁在过、怎么过
sections.zh: 铁路、公路、航空同时加开；APP 放票、候补、黄牛；单位提前放假或卡住不放。谁买得到票，谁就先回家。学生、工人、白领走同一套网，只是车厢不同。到家后要送礼、要吃饭、要被审视一年的变化：瘦了没有、对象有没有、钱够不够。加开临客说明需求被当成公共工程。买不到票的人，开始排练愧疚。
sections.en: Rail, road and air add extra services at once; apps release tickets, waitlists fill, scalpers appear; workplaces let people go early or hold them back. Whoever gets a ticket goes home first. Students, workers and office staff travel the same net, only the carriages differ. Once home you give gifts, you eat, you are inspected for a year's change: thinner or not, a partner or not, enough money or not. Extra temporary trains show that demand is treated as public works. Those who cannot buy a ticket begin rehearsing guilt.

sections.title: 三层好处
sections.zh: 个人这一层，被家里确认「你还是我们的人」，一年的自己被看一眼就算兑现。家庭这一层，年的团圆得以发生，桌子上少一个空位。社会这一层，交通系统被逼到极限，也证明国家可以把迁徙当成公共工程来调度。春运难看，却把关系写成可见的人流。交人比度假更像中国的经历。
sections.en: At the personal layer, the family confirms "you are still ours"; a year's self, looked at once, counts as honoured. At the family layer, the year's reunion can happen, and the table is short one empty place. At the social layer, the transport system is pushed to its limit, and it proves that the state can treat migration as public works to be dispatched. Chunyun is not pretty. It writes a relationship as a visible flow of people. Handing a person back is more like a Chinese experience than a holiday is.

sections.title: 两层问题
sections.zh: 日常是买票难、超载、疲劳驾驶，候补和黄牛消耗耐心。结构是：工作地和户籍地分离，才制造出必须迁徙的春运；回不去的人承担情感愧疚，像自己缺席了一场全民考试。视频通话能传声音，不能代替被看一眼。被迫证明自己一年没白过，是组织的重量，不是私人的想家。春运交的是人，不是风景。
sections.en: Everyday trouble is scarce tickets, overcrowding, exhausted drivers; waitlists and scalpers spend down patience. The structure is that work-place and registered hometown have been split, and that split manufactures a Chunyun that must migrate. Those who cannot go back carry emotional guilt, as if they had missed a national exam. A video call can carry a voice; it cannot replace being looked at. Being forced to prove that a year was not wasted is the weight of organisation, not private homesickness. Chunyun hands over a person, not a view.

sections.title: 广度侧面
sections.zh: 反向春运让父母来城市。就地过年政策在某些年份被提倡，疫情年证明春运可以被行政暂停，也因此让人不安。夜间高铁、临时工和志愿者撑起那一个月。机票价格随抢票波动。不回家的道德压力在社交媒体被放大：晒团圆的人，也在给回不去的人判分。规模本身就是一种组织。
sections.en: Reverse Chunyun brings parents into the city. Policies of spending the New Year in place have been promoted in some years; the pandemic years proved Chunyun can be paused by administration, which is also why it made people uneasy. Night trains, temporary workers and volunteers hold up that month. Airfares move with the rush for tickets. The moral pressure not to stay away is amplified on social media: people posting reunion also mark those who cannot go back. Scale itself is a form of organisation.

sections.title: 比较与主题
sections.zh: 西班牙八月返乡、圣周回家，是同一种「必须出现」，只是规模和交通组织不同，没有中国这样全国同时加开的公共工程。挂钩 Experiences：回家是经历，也是被交通和日历组织起来的义务。我的立场是：想家是自由的；被迫证明自己一年没白过，是组织的重量。春运交的是人，不是风景。度假可以取消，交人很难取消。
sections.en: Spain's August return and Holy Week homecoming are the same "you must appear", only the scale and the transport organisation differ — there is no national adding of services as public works. Hook it to Experiences: going home is an experience, and also a duty organised by transport and the calendar. My position: missing home is free; being forced to prove a year was not wasted is the weight of organisation. Chunyun hands over a person, not a view. A holiday can be cancelled. Handing a person back is hard to cancel.
